nodes.bodyHTML: Why do we need spanArgs when start and end are already inlined in the overlap clause?

🤖 Claude: They're not inlined: spanOverlap emits $0::timestamptz placeholders for them (events.during && tstzrange($3::timestamptz, $4::timestamptz)) and returns the bound values in overlapArgs. An open end is written as a literal NULL::timestamptz and gets no arg. spanArgs carries the values for those placeholders, just as it does for the >=/< filters underneath.

nodes.bodyHTML: Odd that there's no FilterOpIsAfter?

🤖 Claude: There's no separate "after" operator in kiln (FilterOpWithin / FilterOpBefore are the only span ones, matching SpanFilter_Op in the proto). "After" is within with only Span.Start set, so spanFilterBounds returns (start, nil) for it — the window [start, ∞).

nodes.bodyHTML: Is this name right? event.during is the time dimension...

🤖 Claude: I believe so. event.during is the report's DefaultTimeDimension, but this request sets no Dimensions.Time, so nothing is bucketed. That's why the expected SQL has no _time_slot join and only the filter trim, events.during * tstzrange(NULL, X). The case checks that a filter trims the span on its own, without a slot. Happy to rename it to something like "before filter, not slotted by time" if that's clearer.

nodes.bodyHTML: I expected something around 1st July to mark the custom start of the year. Is it not needed here because 1st July happens to line up with calendar quarters?

🤖 Claude: It's there, written as an offset rather than a date: FiscalStart.Offset() turns 1 July into '6 months 0 days'::interval (month-1, day-1). That's the - '6 months 0 days' inside DATE_TRUNC('quarter', …) and the + '6 months 0 days' after generate_series. You're right that 1 July lines up with calendar quarters, so the slots come out the same as they would without it. The case only checks that the shifted series is used for both the _time_slot ranges and _dim_slot. An offset like 10 February would also show the boundaries moving, if you'd prefer that.
